title: NVIDIA Q3 FY27: $115.8B revenue, $7.8B above its own guide, in Kress's first report
subtitle: Data center revenue hit $107.6 billion, Q4 guide moved to $130 billion, and the first results under the new interim CEO eased the leadership-transition overhang.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: NVIDIA reported fiscal Q3 2027 results after the close on November 17, 2026, with revenue of $115.8 billion — up 103% year over year and $7.8 billion above the company's own August guidance of $108 billion. Data center revenue was $107.6 billion, up 110%. GAAP diluted EPS was $2.70 and non-GAAP was $2.68, against a Visible Alpha consensus near $2.47. The company guided Q4 to $130 billion plus or minus 3%, with 71% to 72% gross margin and no China data center compute revenue included. NVIDIA returned $28.1 billion to shareholders in the quarter and has $227.3 billion remaining under buyback authorization.

The number that actually matters is the guide. $130 billion for Q4 keeps the full-year trajectory on the curve Wall Street had modeled before Jensen Huang's November 12 resignation — the event that put a 20% drag on the stock going into the print. Colette Kress, interim CEO while also staying CFO, used the call to make the capital-return story (ongoing buybacks against record free cash flow) the counterweight to the governance uncertainty.

This print lands against two context pieces that have shaped AI markets all month: the New York Fed's November 13 Financial Stability Report, in which 87% of market contacts named AI as the top risk to the financial system, and the Anthropic IPO pricing tonight. Both make NVIDIA the single hinge name for whether the hyperscaler capex cycle holds through 2027. A $130 billion Q4 says it does — at least on the demand side.

For learners: AI infrastructure is the only part of the stack where supply is the binding constraint, not demand. When NVIDIA guides $130 billion for a single quarter with China excluded, read it as the ceiling of what the rest of the industry — hyperscalers, sovereign funds, labs — can actually spend on compute right now. Everything else in AI runs downstream of that number.
